title: Close CRM implementation and setup | Stacktik
metaDescription: Close CRM implementation by Stacktik: pipeline, data migration, calling, sequences and reporting set up, and your sales team trained on it.
h1: Close CRM implementation, set up around how your team sells.
lede: Close CRM implementation is the work of putting Close, a sales CRM with calling and email built in, into daily use: the pipeline, your data, the sequences, the reporting and the people who use it. Stacktik, a RevOps (revenue operations) consultancy in Woodbridge, Ontario, sets Close up as a scoped project for a fixed fee, quoted in writing before work starts.

summary.label: What it is
summary.text: Setting up Close for a sales team: pipeline and rules, data moved in, calling and email sequences working, reporting built, and the team trained.

summary.label: Who it is for
summary.text: Sales teams that work mostly by phone and email and have chosen Close, are weighing it, or have it but never set it up properly.

summary.label: What you get
summary.text: Close configured in your own account, your data moved in with duplicates merged, sequences and routing working, recorded training and written handover notes.

summary.label: How it is priced
summary.text: A fixed fee for the implementation, quoted in writing before work starts. Close stays on its own plan and pricing. The first call is free.

blocks.h2: What a Close CRM implementation covers.
blocks.intro: Every project is scoped on the proposal, so this is the list we draw from, not a fixed package. Smaller fixes to a Close account you already run draw from the same list.

items.title: Pipeline and stage rules
items.body: Pipeline stages that match how a deal really moves, with written rules for when it moves forward. Custom fields are kept to the ones your team will fill in.

items.title: Your data moved in
items.body: Leads, contacts, opportunities and history moved from your current system or spreadsheets, with duplicates merged. The old system stays read-only during the switch, then it is yours to close.

items.title: Calling set up
items.body: Numbers, users and call settings arranged so calls are placed from the record and logged to it with the recording. If you run a separate phone system, we connect it to the CRM.

items.title: Email sequences and their rules
items.body: Sequences your reps send from their own inboxes, with the rules that stop them when a reply comes in. We build the sequence. Your team writes and sends the copy.

items.title: Lead routing
items.body: New leads assigned in turn, by territory, or to whoever is on duty, so a form submission becomes a record with an owner.

items.title: Reporting and the scoreboard
items.body: The reports the owner actually reads, and a revenue scoreboard with targets and a leaderboard, pulled from the CRM without anyone typing.

blocks.h2: When Close CRM fits, and when it does not.
blocks.intro: Close suits some sales teams well and others poorly. We say which on the first call, and the proposal can shortlist a second CRM beside it with the monthly cost of each.

items.title: A team that sells by phone and email
items.body: Close is built around calling and emailing from inside the CRM. A team that spends its day in conversations gets the most from it.

items.title: A team without a full-time admin
items.body: A simpler system is easier to keep clean. If nobody on your team will own the CRM day to day, fewer moving parts is the safer choice.

items.title: When a broader platform fits better
items.body: If marketing, service and sales all need to work in one system, a broader CRM such as HubSpot may be the better shortlist. Stacktik sets up both.

items.title: Close CRM pricing, in structure
items.body: Close is priced per user on its own plans and billed by Close, with separate charges for phone numbers, calls and texts. The proposal shows the monthly plan cost for your seat count. No figures are published here because plans change.

items.title: Close CRM integrations
items.body: Close connects to other tools through its own integrations, through a connector such as Zapier, or through a custom connector we build. The proposal says which route each connection takes.

blocks.h2: How Stacktik runs a Close CRM implementation.
blocks.intro: One technical RevOps consultant is assigned to your project and stays with it. The steps and their order are written on the proposal. This is the usual outline.

items.title: A free call
items.body: We go through how leads, calls and follow-ups move through your team today, what you use, and what isn't working. You get a straight answer on the right next step. No obligation.

items.title: A written proposal
items.body: What to keep, connect or replace, the monthly cost of each tool, and our fee for the work, fixed before it starts. Our relationship with each vendor is stated next to its price.

items.title: Setup in your account
items.body: We work inside your own Close account through an admin seat you create for us and revoke at handover. Pipeline, fields, routing and sequences are set up first.

items.title: Data moved and tools connected
items.body: Your records are moved in and checked against the source. Calling, outreach and reporting are connected and tested with real examples from your team.

items.title: Training and handover
items.body: Training sessions on your own data, recorded for the team. Handover notes say how each piece runs and who to call. Ongoing support is optional and monthly.

platforms.h2: Close and the tools we connect to it.
platforms.intro: Close is one of the CRMs Stacktik sets up. These are the calling, outreach, automation and reporting tools we connect to a CRM. The proposal names the ones that fit you.

faq.a: Close is a sales CRM made for teams that sell by phone and email. Calling and email work from inside the CRM, so conversations are logged on the record as they happen. Stacktik lists Close among the CRMs it sets up, alongside HubSpot, monday.com CRM, Nutshell, Capsule and HighLevel.

faq.q: How much does a Close CRM implementation cost?
faq.a: It is a fixed fee, quoted in writing before work starts, and it depends on scope: how much data moves, how many tools connect, and whether automation or AI agents are part of it. Close itself is billed by Close on its own plans. The proposal shows both numbers separately. Nothing is charged for the first call.

faq.q: Can you set up a Close account we already have?
faq.a: Yes. The proposal says what to keep, what to connect and what, if anything, to rebuild. Smaller improvements to an existing setup draw from the same list as a full implementation, and they are quoted the same way, as a fixed fee in writing.

faq.q: Do we have to buy Close through Stacktik?
faq.a: No. You can buy Close direct and hire us only for the implementation, or buy through us and run the setup yourself. Where a vendor program helps, the proposal says so and states our relationship with the vendor next to the price.

faq.q: Which tools integrate with Close CRM?
faq.a: Close has its own integrations, and many other tools can be connected through Zapier or a custom connector. Stacktik connects calling, email outreach, conversation notes, reporting and AI agents to the CRM, and documents each connection so your team knows how it runs.

faq.q: How do you move our data into Close?
faq.a: We map your fields to Close, clean the data, merge duplicates, run a test import and check it against the source before the final move. The old system stays read-only during the switch. Salesforce and ERP migrations are not usually in scope, so ask on the call if that is where your data lives.

closeH2: Start with how your team sells today.
closeLede: A free call about what you use and what isn't working. You get a straight answer on whether Close fits, and a written proposal if it does.
